**Digne Cathedral** (French: _Cathédrale Saint-Jérome de Digne_) is a Latin Catholicchurch located in the town of Digne-les-Bains, France. The cathedral has been a _monument historique_ since 1906.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne_Cathedral#cite_note-1) It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and Sisteron, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Digne Cathedral, west front
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town's population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, **Notre-Dame-du-Bourg** (_Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne_), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.

The Saint Jerome Cathedral of Digne, located in Digne-les-Bains in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, replaced the former episcopal seat of Notre-Dame-du-Bourg starting in the 16th century. Its construction, initiated in 1490 by Antoine de Guiramand and carried out by Antoine Brollion, was completed by Antoine-Nicolas Bailly between 1846 and 1862 with the addition of a bay and a Gothic-style facade. Pierre Boulanger created the wrought ironwork in 1853. The cathedral houses a listed Cavaillé-Coll gallery organ from 1865 and a bell dating from 1618.

The Saint Jerome Cathedral of Digne, located in Digne-les-Bains in the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, replaced the former episcopal seat of Notre-Dame-du-Bourg starting in the 16th century. Its construction, initiated in 1490 by Antoine de Guiramand and carried out by Antoine Brollion, was completed by Antoine-Nicolas Bailly between 1846 and 1862 with the addition of a bay and a Gothic-style facade. Pierre Boulanger created the wrought ironwork in 1853. The cathedral houses a listed Cavaillé-Coll gallery organ from 1865 and a bell dating from 1618.

**Digne Cathedral** (French: _Cathédrale Saint-Jérome de Digne_) is a Latin Catholicchurch located in the town of Digne-les-Bains, France. The cathedral has been a _monument historique_ since 1906.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne_Cathedral#cite_note-1) It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and Sisteron, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Digne Cathedral, west front
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town's population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, **Notre-Dame-du-Bourg** (_Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne_), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.

**Digne Cathedral** (French: _Cathédrale Saint-Jérome de Digne_) is a Latin Catholicchurch located in the town of Digne-les-Bains, France. The cathedral has been a _monument historique_ since 1906.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne_Cathedral#cite_note-1) It is the seat of the Bishops of Digne, Riez and Sisteron, formerly Bishops of Digne.
Digne Cathedral, west front
Construction began in 1490 by the order of the then bishop Antoine de Guiramand to cater for the movement of the town's population to a higher, more secure and defensible location round the local castle. The cathedral was renovated and expanded in the 1860s under the direction of architect Antoine-Nicolas Bailly.
The previous cathedral in the old town, **Notre-Dame-du-Bourg** (_Cathédrale Notre-Dame-du-Bourg de Digne_), a late Romanesque building of the 13th century, still stands as a museum.

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.

## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
An arrondissement is made up of smaller parts called _cantons_ and _communes_. Think of them like smaller towns and their surrounding areas.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
### Cantons
After some changes in France, cantons are no longer just inside one arrondissement. This means a canton might include small towns (communes) that belong to different arrondissements.
In the Digne-les-Bains arrondissement, there are 6 cantons. Four of these cantons have all their communes completely inside this arrondissement:
*   Digne-les-Bains-1  
*   Digne-les-Bains-2  
*   Oraison (partly in this arrondissement)  
*   Riez  
*   Seyne (partly in this arrondissement)  
*   Valensole

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
### Communes
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement has 46 _communes_. A commune is the smallest type of local government area in France, like a town or a village.

Digne-les-Bains is a French town located in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region and the administrative center of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department, inhabited by the Dignois. It is situated at the geographical center of the department, bordering the Préalpes de Digne, on both sides of the Bléone river, and extends over more than 8 km in length following the annexation of neighboring municipalities. The town center is at an altitude of 608 meters, and the town is surrounded by rugged terrain, with the old town built on a hill between the Bléone and the Eaux-Chaudes stream. The municipality is at the heart of a geological reserve, characterized by hot springs used since antiquity for their healing properties, linked to their rise along Triassic levels. Mont du Cousson is visible, and numerous reliefs offer hiking opportunities. Digne-les-Bains is crossed by the Vallée des Eaux-Chaudes and several tributaries of the Bléone, and its climate is of the altered Mediterranean type or temperate with hot, dry summers. The town is connected to Nice by the Chemins de fer de Provence and has six urban bus lines. It is also exposed to natural risks such as floods, landslides and earthquakes.

**Digne-les-Bains** (French pronunciation:[[diɲ le bɛ̃]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")ⓘ; Occitan: _Dinha dei Banhs_), or simply and historically **Digne** (_Dinha_ in the classical norm or _Digno_ in the Mistralian norm), is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment in the [Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provence-Alpes-C%C3%B4te_d'Azur "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur")region of southern France. Located on the edge of the Digne Prealps and on both sides of the river Bléone, which flows southwest through the middle of the commune and crosses the town; it forms part of the commune's northeastern and southwestern borders.
Digne-les-Bains is the capital of the Department of Alpes de Haute-Provence. Placed in the geographical centre of the Department, the commune is home to 17,400 inhabitants, making it one of the smaller prefectures of France by its population. The town centre is at 608 metres (1,995 ft) altitude.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-LaTorre-3)

Digne is a sprawling commune in the plain formed around the Bléone Valley, given that the terrain that surrounds it is very rugged. The old town is built on a hill between the Bléone and the torrent of the hot springs, but the town has gradually extended in the three directions of the valleys, especially downstream. Its geographical location is quite remarkable, given that it lies at the edge of the Prealps, on a thrust fault that bears its name. A part of the town is completely enclosed in the Bléone Valley, while the town extends widely, on a gentler relief, downstream. With the annexation of neighbouring towns, especially downstream, the town extends over 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in length.

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.

## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

## History of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department was created a long time ago, in 1800. The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement was one of the first parts of this new department.

## Geography of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
The Digne-les-Bains arrondissement is located in the middle of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provence department. It shares borders with other areas:
*   To the north, it borders the Barcelonnette arrondissement.  
*   To the east, it borders the Castellane arrondissement.  
*   To the south, it borders the Var department.  
*   To the west, it borders the Forcalquier arrondissement.
This arrondissement is the biggest in the department by land size. It covers about 2,465.5 square kilometers (951.9 square miles). However, it is the second largest in terms of how many people live there. In 2014, about 55,758 people lived in Digne-les-Bains. The Forcalquier arrondissement has more people.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
An arrondissement is made up of smaller parts called _cantons_ and _communes_. Think of them like smaller towns and their surrounding areas.

## Parts of Digne-les-Bains Arrondissement
### Cantons
After some changes in France, cantons are no longer just inside one arrondissement. This means a canton might include small towns (communes) that belong to different arrondissements.
In the Digne-les-Bains arrondissement, there are 6 cantons. Four of these cantons have all their communes completely inside this arrondissement:
*   Digne-les-Bains-1  
*   Digne-les-Bains-2  
*   Oraison (partly in this arrondissement)  
*   Riez

**Digne-les-Bains** (French pronunciation:[[diɲ le bɛ̃]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")ⓘ; Occitan: _Dinha dei Banhs_), or simply and historically **Digne** (_Dinha_ in the classical norm or _Digno_ in the Mistralian norm), is the prefecture of the Alpes-de-Haute-Provencedepartment in the [Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provence-Alpes-C%C3%B4te_d'Azur "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur")region of southern France. Its inhabitants are called _Dignois_ (masculine) and _Dignoises_ (feminine).
Digne-les-Bains and neighboring municipalities
Located on the edge of the Digne Prealps and on both sides of the river Bléone, which flows southwest through the middle of the commune and crosses the town; it forms part of the commune's northeastern and southwestern borders.
Digne-les-Bains is the capital of the Department of Alpes de Haute-Provence. Placed in the geographical centre of the Department, the commune is home to 17,400 inhabitants, making it one of the smaller prefectures of France by its population. The town centre is at 608 metres (1,995 ft) altitude.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-LaTorre-3)

Digne is a sprawling commune in the plain formed around the Bléone Valley, given that the terrain that surrounds it is very rugged. The old town is built on a hill between the Bléone and the torrent of the hot springs, but the town has gradually extended in the three directions of the valleys, especially downstream. Its geographical location is quite remarkable, given that it lies at the edge of the Prealps, on a thrust fault that bears its name. A part of the town is completely enclosed in the Bléone Valley, while the town extends widely, on a gentler relief, downstream. With the annexation of neighbouring towns, especially downstream, the town extends over 8 kilometres (5.0 mi) in length.

[edit]
The communes surrounding Digne-les-Bains are La Robine-sur-Galabre, Le Brusquet, Marcoux, Archail, Tartonne, Clumanc, Chaudon-Norante, Châteauredon, Le Chaffaut-Saint-Jurson, Aiglun, Champtercier and Thoard.
Digne-les-Bains features a mid-latitude humid subtropical climate (Köppen climate classification: _Cfa_), with mediterranean (_Csa_) and oceanic (_Cfb_) influences. Summers are hot and relatively dry, and winters are mildly cold and relatively wet, with air frosts being regular in the winter months.

### Geology and terrain
[edit]
The commune, which is at the heart of the geology, has its specificities related to the ancient town _[clarification needed_] built upstream of the cluse which the Bléone has worn into the _Nappe de Digne_ to emerge into the tertiary basin of Valensole.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The districts of the town cover the alluvium of the streams which converge upstream of the Cluse. The most eastern suburbs joined a line of limestone hills with flint of the Carixian age, forming russet cliffs oriented to the south-west.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5) The hot springs were captured, since ancient times, to the point where these carixian limestones are cut by the hack of the southernmost valley, descending from Entrages. Their healing powers are linked to their ascent along the gypsiferous Triassic levels of the sole thrust of the _Nappe de Digne_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Geol-alp1-5)
The most visible mountain of the commune is Le Cousson at 1,516 metres (4,974 ft); the Bigué rises to 1,653 metres (5,423 ft).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digne-les-Bains#cite_note-Brunet1-6)
